quandoUsar: Asking someone which times of the week they are free, to schedule meetings, on-call shifts, or appointments in one-hour blocks.
Setting up windows that repeat every week, such as business hours or the period when notifications may arrive.
When the result needs to be checked at a glance: the summary alongside merges adjacent blocks into per-day ranges and totals the hours.
quandoEvitar: Use `date-picker` or `date-range-picker` when the choice is calendar dates rather than times that repeat every week.
Use `time-picker` when a single time is enough.
Avoid when precision needs to be finer than one hour: each cell is a full one-hour block, with no half hours or quarter hours.

teclado.acao: Move focus around the grid, one cell at a time.
Select or deselect the focused time slot.
Paint: the destination cell takes the state (selected or not) of the cell focus came from.
Move focus to the first or last day, at the same hour.
Moves through the ready-made presets, “Clear”, and the day buttons (which select or clear a whole day), then enters the grid at the current cell.

acessibilidade: The grid uses `role="grid"` with `aria-multiselectable`; each cell is a `gridcell` with `aria-selected` and a name like “Monday, 9 AM to 10 AM”, and only the current cell is in the Tab order (roving tabindex).
The total hours sit in an `aria-live="polite"` region, the ready-made presets expose `aria-pressed`, and each day header is a button with its own name.
The internal texts (help, “Clear”, “Available”, “Unavailable”, cell names, and the AM/PM clock) are hardcoded in English; only `title`, `days`, and the `presets` labels come through props.
movimento: Each selected slot grows from the center of the cell on a no-overshoot spring curve and disappears with a simple fade; in batch changes (preset, whole day) the cells fill in a wave from the origin.
The total hours change by scrolling: the old number moves up and the new one enters from below, on a no-overshoot spring.
With “reduce motion” on, cell and button transitions are turned off and the total changes instantly.
responsivo: Uses a container query: below 46rem of block width the summary drops below the grid, and below 30rem the days show only the initial.
The grid body has `touch-action: none`: on touch, dragging over the slots selects them instead of scrolling the page, so leave free space around it for scrolling.
desempenho: Each time slot is one DOM element (`days` × visible hours, 84 by default), and during a drag the state changes only when the pointer enters another cell, not on every pixel.
notasIA: Controlled with `value` and `onValueChange`: the selection is a list of `"dia-hora"` ids, with the day counted from 0 and the hour on a 24-hour clock (`"0-9"` is the first day at 9 AM).
Without `value` or `defaultValue`, the grid starts with the first five columns selected from 9 AM to 5 PM, except noon; pass `defaultValue={[]}` to start empty.
`startHour` and `endHour` define the rows (8 and 20 by default), `days` the columns, and `presets` the shortcuts, each with a `label` and an `includes(day, hour)` function.
